summary: This meta-analysis investigated the correlation between retinal thickness and hippocampal volume in Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) individuals, and normal controls (NC) using optical coherence tomography (OCT) images and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Nine studies were included, revealing a positive moderate correlation between retinal thickness and hippocampal volume in all participants, with the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (pRNFL) showing the strongest correlation. The study found that retinal thickness was positively correlated with hippocampal volume in both NC and AD groups, particularly in MCI individuals.
